literal: All his contemporaries admired his clear understanding, and he became renowned for his medical skill as well.
idiomatic: Contemporaries admired his keen understanding, and he won fame as a physician besides.

literal: Missing: at the end of Wei he served as adjutant to the Defender-in-Chief and as Governor of Wuyi.
idiomatic: [Text missing.] At the end of Wei he served as adjutant to the defender-in-chief and as governor of Wuyi.

literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao he served as chief clerk to the minister of works.

literal: During Daning and Wuping he was Administrator of Qinghe and Guangping and held the title Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the Silver Seal.
idiomatic: During the Daning and Wuping eras he governed Qinghe and Guangping and held the title grand master for splendid happiness with the silver seal.

literal: He died after the fall of Qi.
idiomatic: He died after Qi fell.

literal: His son Daoqian, during Wuping, was Investigating Censor.
idiomatic: His son Daoqian served as investigating censor during Wuping.

literal: Daoqian's younger brother Daozhen was Adjutant of Southern Qing Province and was killed by the rebel Xing Guo.
idiomatic: Daoqian's younger brother Daozhen was adjutant of Southern Qing Province and was killed by the rebel Xing Guo.

literal: Posthumously granted Governor of Northern Xu Province.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted governor of Northern Xu Province.

literal: Min, a clansman of Yuanzhong, styled Molian, was of towering build and striking appearance, unlike any man of his age.
idiomatic: Min, a clansman of Yuanzhong, styled Molian, was a man of towering build and striking mien — unlike anyone else of his day.

literal: From youth he nursed great ambitions. Even at forty he still would not take office in prefecture or commandery, but gathered rogues and daredevils as his companions.
idiomatic: From youth he nursed great ambitions. Even at forty he would not serve in prefecture or commandery, gathering rogues and daredevils as his companions instead.

literal: At the end of Xiaochang, when warfare erupted across the realm, Min withdrew to Mount Linlu and watched for the turn of events.
idiomatic: At the end of the Xiaochang era, as warfare erupted across the realm, Min withdrew to Mount Linlu and watched for the turn of events.

literal: The bandit chiefs Xianyu Xiuli and Mao Puxian rose in rebellion. An edict dispatched Grand Commander Changsun Zhi to suppress them.
idiomatic: The bandit chiefs Xianyu Xiuli and Mao Puxian rose in rebellion, and an edict dispatched Grand Commander Changsun Zhi to suppress them.

literal: Zhi had long heard of Min's reputation and summoned him to serve concurrently as commander of the tent guard.
idiomatic: Zhi had long heard of Min's reputation and summoned him to serve concurrently as commander of the tent guard.

literal: When the army reached Hutuo, the rebels came out to give battle. Zhi's army was defeated by the rebels, and Min returned home.
idiomatic: When the army reached Hutuo, the rebels came out to fight. Zhi's army was routed, and Min returned home.

literal: Prince Yuan of Anle served as Grand Mobile Office of the Northern Circuit. When he reached Ye, the rebel forces were so strong that he could not advance.
idiomatic: Prince Yuan of Anle served as grand mobile office of the northern circuit. When he reached Ye, the rebels were so strong that he could not advance.

literal: He sent envoys to summon Min and memorialized the throne to appoint him Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, with provisional staff and separate command, garrisoning the eastern suburb of Ye.
idiomatic: He sent envoys to summon Min and memorialized the throne to appoint him cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, with provisional staff and separate command, garrisoning the eastern suburb of Ye.

literal: When Ge Rong besieged Xindu, his remnant bands raided southward, and all lands north of Yangping fell into rebel hands.
idiomatic: When Ge Rong besieged Xindu, his remnant bands raided southward until all lands north of Yangping lay in rebel hands.

literal: Yuan ordered Min to serve as vanguard and separately suppress them; he won considerable heads and captives.
idiomatic: Yuan ordered Min to serve as vanguard and hunt them down separately; he took many heads and captives.

literal: When Yuan plotted rebellion, Min feigned a sudden fit of wind sickness. Yuan believed him and thus Min escaped harm.
idiomatic: When Yuan plotted rebellion, Min feigned a sudden fit of wind sickness. Yuan believed him, and Min escaped harm.

literal: Not long after, Grand Commander Yuan Ziyong encamped at Anyang and Grand Commander Pei Yan encamped at Ye; together they marched west to attack Yuan.
idiomatic: Not long after, Grand Commander Yuan Ziyong encamped at Anyang and Grand Commander Pei Yan at Ye; together they marched west against Yuan.

literal: Min abandoned his family and fled to Ziyong, then was summoned to the capital and made Keeper of the Imperial Carriages, with staff of authority garrisoning Zhihe.
idiomatic: Min abandoned his family and fled to Ziyong, then was summoned to the capital and made keeper of the imperial carriages, with staff of authority garrisoning Zhihe.

literal: Zhihe lay northwest of Ye, in the heart of the mountains, on the border between Bing and Xiang provinces.
idiomatic: Zhihe lay northwest of Ye, deep in the mountains, on the border between Bing and Xiang provinces.

literal: Because Ge Rong was pressing south, Min was posted there.
idiomatic: Because Ge Rong was pressing south, Min was posted there.

literal: Ge Rong sent his uncle, Prince Ge of Leling, with ten thousand elite cavalry to attack Min. Min held the defiles and fought them off; Ge could not advance.
idiomatic: Ge Rong sent his uncle, Prince Ge of Leling, with ten thousand elite cavalry to attack Min. Min held the defiles and fought them off, and Ge could not advance.

literal: When Erzhu Rong reached Dongguan, Min went to see him.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong reached Dongguan, Min went to see him.

literal: Rong wished to divide the rebel forces and sent Min by a separate route toward Xiangguo to strike the army of Tian Hu, whom the rebels had appointed Provisional Governor of Guang Province.
idiomatic: Rong wished to divide the rebel forces and sent Min by a separate route toward Xiangguo to strike the army of Tian Hu, whom the rebels had appointed provisional governor of Guang Province.

literal: Before Min reached Xiangguo, Ge Rong had already been captured.
idiomatic: Before Min reached Xiangguo, Ge Rong had already been captured.

literal: He was immediately memorialized for appointment as General Who Establishes Loyalty.
idiomatic: He was immediately memorialized for appointment as general who establishes loyalty.

literal: The three counties of Yiyang, Xiangguo, and Zhongqiu — drawn from Guangping and Southern Zhao commanderies — were joined into Yiyang Commandery, and Min was made its Administrator.
idiomatic: The three counties of Yiyang, Xiangguo, and Zhongqiu — taken from Guangping and Southern Zhao commanderies — were joined into Yiyang Commandery, and Min was made its administrator.

literal: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiangguo.
idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as marquis of Xiangguo.

literal: At the end of Yongan he was made acting General Who Pacifies the North, with staff of authority and grand governorship of the commandery, and transferred to Administrator of Leping.
idiomatic: At the end of Yongan he was made acting general who pacifies the north, with staff of authority and grand governorship of the commandery, and transferred to administrator of Leping.

literal: Before he reached the commandery, Luoyang fell. Min led his troops west to hold Shimen Mountain.
idiomatic: Before he reached the commandery, Luoyang fell. Min led his troops west to hold Shimen Mountain.

literal: Secretly he entered into covenant with Liu Lingzhu, Governor of You Province, the Gao brothers of Ganyu, Lu Cao, Governor of An Province, and others to raise the righteous banner together.
idiomatic: Secretly he entered into covenant with Liu Lingzhu, governor of You Province, the Gao brothers of Ganyu, Lu Cao, governor of An Province, and others to raise the righteous banner together.

literal: When Lingzhu was defeated, Min withdrew into Shimen.
idiomatic: When Lingzhu was defeated, Min withdrew into Shimen.

literal: When Gao Huan raised the righteous cause, he wrote to summon Min. Min answered the letter and came with several thousand followers to join Gao Huan, who personally went out to welcome him.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan raised the righteous cause, he wrote to summon Min. Min answered the letter and came with several thousand followers; Gao Huan personally went out to welcome him.

literal: He was made Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General Who Campaigns South, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in Xiang Province, and Governor of Xiang Province, and concurrently Director of the Southwest Circuit Mobile Office and Grand Governor of the Province.
idiomatic: He was made bearer of the staff of authority, general who campaigns south, commander-in-chief of military affairs in Xiang Province, and governor of Xiang Province, and concurrently director of the southwest circuit mobile office and grand governor of the province.

literal: Min was ordered to lead his original forces back to his old post; Gao Huan personally saw him off.
idiomatic: Min was ordered to lead his original forces back to his old post, and Gao Huan personally saw him off.

literal: When Min reached his home district, he took Mount Ma'an, built fortifications in the defiles, levied grain, and gathered troops to make a show of strength.
idiomatic: When Min reached his home district, he took Mount Ma'an, built fortifications in the defiles, levied grain, and gathered troops to make a show of strength.

literal: Erzhu Zhao came out through Jingxing Pass, and Gao Huan defeated him at Guang'a.
idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao came out through Jingxing Pass, and Gao Huan defeated him at Guang'a.

literal: Min commanded his original forces and encamped at the old city to guard against Erzhu Zhao.
idiomatic: Min commanded his original forces and encamped at the old city to guard against Erzhu Zhao.

literal: Once Xiang Province was pacified, Min was ordered back to Ye and made Director of the Masters of Writing for the Southwest Circuit Mobile Office, again encamping at the old city.
idiomatic: Once Xiang Province was pacified, Min was ordered back to Ye and made director of the masters of writing for the southwest circuit mobile office, again encamping at the old city.

literal: When Erzhu Zhao and the others were about to arrive, Gao Huan summoned Min to help defend Ye.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao and the others were about to arrive, Gao Huan summoned Min to help defend Ye.

literal: At the beginning of Taichang he was made Director of the Imperial Treasuries.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Taichang he was made director of the imperial treasuries.

literal: Later he went out as Governor of Southern Jing Province and Grand Governor of the Province.
idiomatic: Later he went out as governor of Southern Jing Province and grand governor of the province.

literal: Since Xiaochang this province's old routes had been cut off; successive governors had reached it only by hidden paths.
idiomatic: Since Xiaochang the province's old routes had been cut off, and successive governors had reached it only by hidden paths.

literal: Min led several thousand followers of his personal guard straight toward Xuanhu, reopened the old route from Beiyang, and fought his way forward more than three hundred li. Wherever he passed he established postal stations, and the barbarian peoples on the left were deeply impressed.
idiomatic: Min led several thousand followers of his personal guard straight toward Xuanhu, reopened the old route from Beiyang, and fought his way forward more than three hundred li. Wherever he passed he established postal stations, and the frontier peoples were deeply impressed.

literal: Liang sent its Governor of Southern Si Province Ren Sinzu, Administrator of Suixian Huan He, and others with thirty thousand infantry and cavalry, and also mobilized frontier barbarians, to surround and press the garrison at Xiazhao.
idiomatic: Liang sent its governor of Southern Si Province Ren Sinzu, administrator of Suixian Huan He, and others with thirty thousand infantry and cavalry, and also mobilized frontier barbarians, to surround and press the garrison at Xiazhao.

literal: Min personally led the counterattack and routed them.
idiomatic: Min personally led the counterattack and routed them.

literal: An edict promoted him to General of Chariots and Cavalry.
idiomatic: An edict promoted him to general of chariots and cavalry.

literal: Within the province Min opened dams and channels and irrigated more than a thousand qing of rice fields; public and private interests alike depended on this.
idiomatic: Within the province Min opened dams and channels and irrigated more than a thousand qing of rice fields, to the benefit of public and private alike.

literal: He was transferred to Eastern Jing Province and additionally made General Who Conquers on Horseback, Governor of Eastern Jing Province, Grand Governor of the Province, and Regular Attendant.
idiomatic: He was transferred to Eastern Jing Province and additionally made general who conquers on horseback, governor of Eastern Jing Province, grand governor of the province, and regular attendant.

literal: He died in the second year of Tianping.
idiomatic: He died in the second year of Tianping.

literal: Posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, military affairs of Ding and Yin provinces, Equal in Protocol to Three Imperators, and Governor of Ding Province.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted bearer of the staff of authority, military affairs of Ding and Yin provinces, equal in protocol to three imperators, and governor of Ding Province.

literal: Jingyi, Yuanzhong's clansman by marriage, was fierce and bold in youth, with great physical courage. He loved gathering fugitives and outlaws to rob and plunder together, and the neighborhood suffered from him.
idiomatic: Jingyi, Yuanzhong's clansman by marriage, was fierce and bold in youth, with great physical courage. He loved gathering fugitives and outlaws for robbery and plunder, and the neighborhood suffered from him.

literal: At the end of Yongan, his elder brother Wuwei, Governor of Southern Julu, was impeached by the censorate for corruption and imprisoned in the provincial jail.
idiomatic: At the end of Yongan, his elder brother Wuwei, governor of Southern Julu, was impeached by the censorate for corruption and imprisoned in the provincial jail.

literal: Jingyi led a dozen or so mounted followers, falsely claiming to be imperial envoys, and burst straight into the provincial city, seizing Wuwei and freeing him.
idiomatic: Jingyi led a dozen or so mounted followers, falsely claiming to be imperial envoys, and burst straight into the provincial city to seize Wuwei and free him.

literal: The provincial army pursued and attacked but could not restrain him.
idiomatic: The provincial army pursued and attacked but could not restrain him.

literal: By this he became renowned for chivalry.
idiomatic: By this he became renowned for chivalry.

literal: When Gao Huan raised the righteous cause at Xindu, Jingyi came to the camp gate.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan raised the righteous cause at Xindu, Jingyi came to the camp gate.

literal: Gao Huan had long heard his name and received him with great favor.
idiomatic: Gao Huan had long heard his name and received him with great favor.

literal: He ordered Jingyi together with Yuanzhong to raise troops on the Western Mountains, then join the main army; they captured and executed Governor Erzhu Yusheng.
idiomatic: He ordered Jingyi together with Yuanzhong to raise troops on the Western Mountains and join the main army; they captured and executed Governor Erzhu Yusheng.

literal: For his merit he was made General of the Dragon Cavalry, Duke of Changping County, with a fief of eight hundred households.
idiomatic: For his merit he was made general of the dragon cavalry, duke of Changping County, with a fief of eight hundred households.

literal: When Erzhu Zhao came to attack, he fought vigorously with further merit and was made Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand Commander, and Left General.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao came to attack, he fought vigorously with further merit and was made bearer of the staff of authority, grand commander, and left general.

literal: At the beginning of Taichang his rank was advanced to Duke of Changping Commandery with three hundred additional households, and he was made General of Chariots and Cavalry.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Taichang his rank was advanced to duke of Changping Commandery with three hundred additional households, and he was made general of chariots and cavalry.

literal: At the beginning of Tianping he went out as Governor of Ying Province.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianping he went out as governor of Ying Province.

literal: Not long after, he was ambushed and killed by the former Administrator of Yingchuan, Yuan Hongwei.
idiomatic: Not long after, he was ambushed and killed by the former administrator of Yingchuan, Yuan Hongwei.

literal: Posthumously granted Palace Attendant, military affairs of Yin and Cang provinces, Grand General, Opener of a Government Office, and Governor of Yin Province.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted palace attendant, military affairs of Yin and Cang provinces, grand general, opener of a government office, and governor of Yin Province.

literal: His son Qialin succeeded.
idiomatic: His son Qialin succeeded.

literal: Lu Wenwei, styled Xizu, was a native of Zhuo in Fanyang.
idiomatic: Lu Wenwei, styled Xizu, came from Zhuo in Fanyang.

literal: His clan ranked among the foremost families of the Northern Provinces.
idiomatic: His clan ranked among the foremost families of the northern provinces.

literal: His father Chang was adopted as heir by his uncle Bo Jia.
idiomatic: His father Chang was adopted as heir by his uncle Bo Jia.

literal: Wenwei lost his father early but had lofty aspirations. He read widely in the classics and histories, was devoted to friendship, and in youth was respected by the neighborhood.
idiomatic: Wenwei lost his father early but had lofty aspirations. He read widely in the classics and histories, was devoted to friendship, and in youth was respected throughout the neighborhood.

literal: The province recruited him as chief clerk.
idiomatic: The province recruited him as chief clerk.

literal: At thirty-eight he was first nominated as a Cultivated Talent.
idiomatic: At thirty-eight he was first nominated as a cultivated talent.

literal: He was appointed Chief Adjutant of the Pacifier of the North office in his home province and persuaded Governor Pei Jun to restore the Dukang Dam according to old traces, irrigating more than ten thousand qing of fields to the people's benefit. Most of the construction work was entrusted to Wenwei.
idiomatic: He was appointed chief adjutant of the pacifier of the north office in his home province and persuaded Governor Pei Jun to restore the Dukang Dam according to old traces, irrigating more than ten thousand qing of fields to the people's benefit. Most of the construction work was entrusted to Wenwei.

literal: Since Wenwei excelled at management and also contributed private labor, though his family had been poor and frugal, he grew wealthy thereby.
idiomatic: Wenwei excelled at management and also contributed private labor; though his family had been poor and frugal, he grew wealthy thereby.

literal: In the Xiaochang era an edict appointed him concurrently as Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue; Field Marshal Chang Jing requested that he remain as Bureau Director on the mobile office staff.
idiomatic: In the Xiaochang era an edict appointed him concurrently as bureau director in the ministry of revenue; Field Marshal Chang Jing requested that he remain as bureau director on the mobile office staff.

literal: As the North was on the verge of chaos, Wenwei stockpiled grain in Fanyang city. When famine and dearth struck, he distributed relief generously and won ever greater trust from his neighbors.
idiomatic: As the north was on the verge of chaos, Wenwei stockpiled grain in Fanyang city. When famine and dearth struck, he distributed relief generously and won ever greater trust from his neighbors.

literal: He was soon captured by Du Luozhou.
idiomatic: He was soon captured by Du Luozhou.

literal: When Luozhou was defeated he joined Ge Rong; when Rong was defeated he returned home.
idiomatic: When Luozhou was defeated he joined Ge Rong; when Rong was defeated he returned home.

literal: At that time Han Lou held Jicheng. Wenwei led the neighborhood to hold Fanyang and resist Lou.
idiomatic: At that time Han Lou held Jicheng. Wenwei led the neighborhood to hold Fanyang and resist Lou.

literal: He was then made acting Governor of Fanyang Commandery.
idiomatic: He was then made acting governor of Fanyang Commandery.

literal: For two years he defended the city, sharing hardship with the soldiers, dispersing his family wealth to rescue the destitute; everyone was moved with gratitude.
idiomatic: For two years he defended the city, sharing hardship with the soldiers and dispersing his family wealth to rescue the destitute; everyone was moved with gratitude.

literal: Erzhu Rong sent General Hou Shen to suppress Lou. When Lou was pacified, Wenwei was enfeoffed as Baron of Daxia with two hundred households and made Governor of Fanyang.
idiomatic: Erzhu Rong sent General Hou Shen to suppress Lou. When Lou was pacified, Wenwei was enfeoffed as baron of Daxia with two hundred households and made governor of Fanyang.

literal: Hou Shen remained to garrison Fanyang.
idiomatic: Hou Shen remained to garrison Fanyang.

literal: After Rong was executed, Wenwei knew Shen could not be trusted. He lured him out on a hunt and shut the gates against him.
idiomatic: After Rong was executed, Wenwei knew Shen could not be trusted. He lured him out on a hunt and shut the gates against him.

literal: Shen lost his footing and fled to Zhongshan.
idiomatic: Shen lost his footing and fled to Zhongshan.

literal: When Emperor Zhuang died, Wenwei plotted an uprising together with Liu Lingzhu, Governor of You Province.
idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang died, Wenwei plotted an uprising together with Liu Lingzhu, governor of You Province.

literal: Lingzhu captured Ying Province and left Wenwei to handle affairs while he personally led troops toward Ding Province, but was defeated by Hou Shen, a general of Erzhu Rong. Wenwei abandoned the province and fled back to his home commandery, still acting in concert with the Gao brothers of Ganyu.
idiomatic: Lingzhu captured Ying Province and left Wenwei to handle affairs while he personally led troops toward Ding Province, but was defeated by Hou Shen, a general of Erzhu Rong. Wenwei abandoned the province and fled back to his home commandery, still acting in concert with the Gao brothers of Ganyu.

literal: When Gao Huan reached Xindu, Wenwei sent his son Huaidao with a memorial expressing loyalty; Gao Huan welcomed this favorably.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan reached Xindu, Wenwei sent his son Huaidao with a memorial expressing loyalty, and Gao Huan welcomed it favorably.

literal: At the beginning of Zhongxing he was made General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of An Province.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhongxing he was made general who pacifies the east and governor of An Province.

literal: An Province had not yet submitted, so he remained in the commander's role, handling affairs of You Province, with additional titles as Suppressing-Army General and regular Governor.
idiomatic: An Province had not yet submitted, so he remained in the commander's role, handling affairs of You Province, with additional titles as suppressing-army general and regular governor.

literal: At that time Lu Cao, Governor of An Province, had also raised troops with Lingzhu. When Lingzhu was defeated, Cao seized You Province and surrendered to Erzhu Zhao, who reappointed him governor; Cao held the city and would not submit.
idiomatic: At that time Lu Cao, governor of An Province, had also raised troops with Lingzhu. When Lingzhu was defeated, Cao seized You Province and surrendered to Erzhu Zhao, who reappointed him governor; Cao held the city and would not submit.

literal: Wenwei could not enter the province and established the provincial seat at the commandery capital.
idiomatic: Wenwei could not enter the province and established the provincial seat at the commandery capital.

literal: At the beginning of Taichang he was transferred to Governor of An Province and cumulatively promoted to Regular Attendant.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Taichang he was transferred to governor of An Province and cumulatively promoted to regular attendant.

literal: At the end of Tianping, Gao Huan had Wenwei act for Eastern Yong Province, then transferred him to act for Qing Province.
idiomatic: At the end of Tianping, Gao Huan had Wenwei act for Eastern Yong Province, then transferred him to act for Qing Province.

literal: Wenwei was light with wealth, loved entertaining guests, skilled at winning people over, and fond of small favors; therefore he won considerable goodwill wherever he served. Though he accepted bribes, officials and commoners did not greatly suffer from it.
idiomatic: Wenwei was light with wealth, loved entertaining guests, skilled at winning people over, and fond of small favors; therefore he won considerable goodwill wherever he served. Though he accepted bribes, officials and commoners did not greatly suffer from it.

literal: In managing his livelihood he often seemed to lack enough, yet he amassed wealth, currying favor with the powerful and sending gifts without cease.
idiomatic: In managing his livelihood he often seemed to lack enough, yet he amassed wealth, currying favor with the powerful and sending gifts without cease.

literal: In the third year of Xinghe he died in office at the age of sixty.
idiomatic: In the third year of Xinghe he died in office at the age of sixty.

literal: Posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in Ding, Ying, and Yin provinces, Grand Tutor, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Ding Province; posthumous title Xiaowei.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted bearer of the staff of authority, palace attendant, commander-in-chief of military affairs in Ding, Ying, and Yin provinces, grand tutor, left vice director of the masters of writing, and governor of Ding Province, with the posthumous title Xiaowei.
